hypothesis: Subtracting non-retryable active task claims from autonomy queue actionability will stop duplicate builder dispatch for pending-merge tasks while keeping the blocked task visible in queue payloads.

metricsCompared.name: pending-merge queue dispatch behavior
metricsCompared.baseline: dispatcher and explorer derived queue availability from raw ready/doing counts, so a pending-merge ready task could still look actionable
metricsCompared.candidate: focused tests prove pending-merge ready claims reduce actionability to zero, suppress queue.available and queue.thin, and expose claimBlockedTasks on the empty payload

metricsCompared.name: builder duplicate-claim prevention
metricsCompared.baseline: builder could wake on a queue.available trigger even when the only visible ready task was not claimable
metricsCompared.candidate: builder claim-aware gate test proves claim-task and build skip when the claim-aware snapshot reports zero actionable work

metricsCompared.name: repair gate health
metricsCompared.baseline: post-check repair reported one failing workspace test, missing autonomy-change decision evidence, and a blocking source-size batch with seven warnings
metricsCompared.candidate: focused test suite passes, the workspace test has the missing claim-inspection mock, and the source-size gate is advisory-only with two legacy warnings

rationale: The workflow change is narrow: dispatcher, builder, and explorer now consume a shared claim-aware queue wrapper while the repo-task snapshot contract remains raw. Deterministic tests cover the pending-merge ready-task case, builder skip behavior, dispatcher payload visibility, existing dependency-blocked routing, and the workspaceDir regression from the repair report.
